W2 (empirical), after E025. Tip is E023: 6.198 s, 0.7538 (9.0 true epochs, 225 steps).

Measured chain: E004 compiled 0.7486/9.04. E005 +EMA 0.7583/9.10. E006 +Muon 0.7649/9.45. E007 prog-res 0.7590/7.33. E008 -0.5ep 0.7572/6.98. E010 width 512 0.7548/6.64. E011 aggressive res 0.7451/5.70. E015 CUDA graphs 0.7574/6.58. E016 wd/2 0.7607/6.58. E017 break-free 0.7537/6.548. E018 24/32 only 0.7502/5.99. E019 rerun of E016 code 0.7541/6.54. E020 -1 epoch 0.7528/5.86. E021 group 2 at 320: 0.7530/6.04. E022 0.7545/6.548. E023 -0.5 epoch 0.7538/6.198. E024 26px mid 0.7510/6.07. E025 EMA exponent 2 0.7557/6.20.

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: about 5-5.5% of time per 0.5 epoch (E017→E023 saved 0.35 s). Accuracy cost is small, 0.0-0.15 pp per 0.5 epoch (E020, E023). It is the cheapest lever measured. Time is not strictly linear in epochs, because the step count is quantized.
2. EMA gave +0.97 pp. Muon gave +0.66 pp.
3. Time tracks FLOPs and pixel count. Narrowing group 2 cut 7.8% of time for -0.1 to -0.3 pp. Resolution cuts cost the most accuracy per second saved (E011, E018, E024 at -0.3 pp).
4. wd, label smoothing, Muon lr, LR floor and EMA exponent are flat within noise (E009, E013, E014, E022, E025 at +0.19 pp, unreadable). E016's 0.7607 was noise.
5. CUDA graphs and break removal gave about 1% each. The run is compute-bound.
6. Noise: identical code is bit-identical. Any edit that changes RNG use reshuffles the 3-seed mean by ±0.3 pp. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: I mispredicted time on several trims (it was faster than I expected, E018, E020, E021, E024, E025) and the E016 accuracy. Lesson: time effects are predictable and accuracy deltas under 0.4 pp are unreadable. Treat the true mean of the tip as about 0.753±0.002, so the bar is a coin flip. Further trims land at about 0.751-0.754.

Unsure: whether the held-out mean clears 0.75. Whether batch 2500 gives a free time gain. Whether FreezeOut and drop-easy savings are real after overhead.

forecasts.reason: Diagnostic with no recipe change. Per-layer efficiency likely shows small-map layers at lower efficiency, but nothing is scored. Metrics show the unchanged tip.
0.25 epoch is about 2.7% of time. Accuracy falls about 0.05-0.1 pp, which noise swamps. About a 45% chance it clears 0.753.
The tail saving is real but about 5% at best after two graphs. Freezing group 1 likely costs 0.1-0.3 pp.
The step count falls 9%, but dropping easy examples under strong label smoothing and the topk overhead likely cost more than 0.2 pp. Net it is no better than the epoch dial.
The step is compute-bound, so the saving is only about 1.5% from fewer launches and better utilization. Accuracy falls slightly with 20% fewer steps.
Muon lr has been flat (E014). Time is unchanged. The accuracy change is zero ± 0.3 pp.

cruxes: What is the held-out seeds 3-12 mean of the E023 tip? If it is above 0.7535, more epoch trims are affordable. If it is near 0.751, they are not.
Is per-step time at batch 2000 compute-bound at every resolution? That decides whether batch 2500 or CUDA-graph tweaks save anything.
Does the backward truncation or example dropping save at least 4% net after overhead? Only that would beat the epoch dial at about 5% per 0.5 epoch.
